channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: Twins trade for first baseman Eric Wagaman in deal with Miami Marlins
item.description: Wagaman, 28, hit .250 with nine home runs and 53 RBI in 140 games with the Marlins as a rookie last year.

item.title: Anderson: Forward-facing sonar threatens Minnesota walleyes and other fish
item.description: The DNR should restrict when and where gadgets can be used, one longtime Ely guide says.

item.title: Analysis: Koi Perich was a feel-good story for Gophers, but he seems likely to head for greener pastures
item.description: The team’s star safety entered the transfer portal and will have plenty of options in college football’s strange new world.

item.title: In Minnesota hockey rinks, tariffs hit the boards
item.description: The dasher boards that line ice arenas in Minnesota contain aluminum components from Canada, adding tariff bills of thousands to rink renovations.

item.title: What to know as Minnesota faces another deadline over its high school transgender athlete policy
item.description: U.S. Department of Education determined MN Dept. of Education and MSHSL violated sex discrimination law on Sept. 30.

item.title: Takeaways: Mayor Kaohly Her’s agenda for St. Paul
item.description: The new mayor outlined priorities, from city budget fixes to pushback against immigration enforcement, in her inaugural address.

item.title: Duluth police officer with troubled history no longer with the department
item.description: Tyler Leibfried, who has more than a dozen complaints against him, was out as of Dec. 23.

item.title: Team USA eliminated from World Junior Championship in 4-3 overtime loss to Finland
item.description: Arttu Valila scored in overtime to lift the Finns to victory in a rematch of last year’s gold medal game.

item.title: Minnesota investigates child care centers following fraud accusations
item.description: The Minnesota Department of Children, Youth and Families is investigating four sites highlighted in a viral video claiming fraud in the state’s child care program.

item.title: Small Business Administration bans thousands of Minnesota borrowers over suspected pandemic-era fraud
item.description: The agency’s leader said a review over the past week flagged $400 million in loans to Minnesotans with “suspected fraudulent activity.”
